Q22
Project Description #1 – Describe ONE project, effort, or service provided by the CHC.
Bell CHC worked with the re-established Killeen Area Heritage Association (KAHA) to save and preserve the Bethel Primitive Baptist
Church and Log Cabin, likely the oldest building in Killeen. A Recorded Texas Historic Landmark, it was relocated from the defunct
Palo Alto Community, which pre-dates Killeen's railroad founding. The county provided delayed funding in 2025 for a 2024 request to
repair the church roof, and in 2025, we provided a microgrant to allow KAHA to repair the HVAC to ensure the interior temperature
could be maintained. Our Chair worked with the staff of Preservation Texas to support preservation efforts, which resulted in the
church and cabin being named to their 2025 Most Endangered Places in Texas list. https://www.preservationtexas.org/mep/bethel-
primitive-baptist. Our collaboration with KAHA continues as we move to preserve the log cabin on site and seek new sources and
grants.

Q23
Project Description #2 – Describe ONE project, effort, or service provided by the CHC.
The grant Committee awarded $8,000 in grants for four projects.
1) Josh Hogan Eagle Project received $2,8820 to purchase markers for the historically African American cemetery 7 Star in Temple.
His goal is to fund stone marker replacements for 480 graves.
2) KAHA received a $665 grant for HVAC repairs to the RTHL Primitive Baptist Church
3) Temple Railroad and Heritage Museum reveived $1,800 for special protective frames for historic photographs that will be on display
in the museum.
4) Bartlett Activity Center (est. 1909), which serves as a museum-like site for Bartlett history, received $2,715 to contribute to repairing
the flooring at the historic former school.
We also had unallotted dollars, allowing for an off-cycle grant of $1,600 to the Salado Historical Society for equipment for their 1908
historic church restoration project.

Q24
Project Description #3 – Describe ONE project, effort, or service provided by the CHC.
The Marker Chair worked with the Belton Journal to recognize its upcoming 160 years of continuous operation. The first stage was to
conduct research on the chronology and continuity of the newspaper and connect the name changes to ownership and management in
preparation of an application for a Texas Historical Commission Subject Marker. We worked with the Editor to submit the organization
for the Texas Treasure Business designation, an official designation for long-standing Texas businesses that have made sustained
contributions to their communities and to the state’s economic and cultural history. This was approved in February 2026. In 2026, this
research will be used as part of the application for a Subject Marker.
